summary_paragraph: A male patient with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis and recent coronary stenting was admitted for lower abdominal pain, vomiting, and diarrhea. Initial evaluation revealed elevated cardiac enzymes and EKG changes concerning for NSTEMI, prompting a cardiac catheterization that showed in-stent restenosis of the right coronary artery, which was treated with a new drug-eluting stent. Abdominal CT suggested infectious enterocolitis, and the patient was treated with ciprofloxacin and metronidazole, with resolution of symptoms. Markedly elevated CK levels indicated rhabdomyolysis, likely due to simvastatin, which was discontinued along with colchicine. The patient improved clinically, with decreasing CK and resolution of abdominal symptoms, and was discharged home on dual antiplatelet therapy and antibiotics, with plans for outpatient follow-up and CK monitoring.
